title: 2026 Predictions with Dan Ives and Chris Verrone | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 40
summary: The panel favors continued AI investment and broader market participation while debating power constraints, model economics, interest rates and valuation. Ives emphasizes enterprise adoption and specific AI beneficiaries; Verrone prefers bank leadership, contrarian sectors and price trends; Eisman tests financing, housing supply and conditional AI risks. Primary records support Apple’s Gemini catalyst and Eisman’s resistance to rapid Fed-cut expectations. Some bullish supporting premises are overstated, including enterprise adoption, Oracle backlog timing and Palantir’s sales model. Full-year targets remain open, and first-half rotation lacks matched return verification.
assessment: Substantive outcomes and reasoning are separated from supporting numeric mistakes. Eisman asks informative falsification questions and explicitly withholds a Tesla investment, but broad enthusiasm does not define a measurable portfolio return. Full-year and multiyear forecasts retain open horizons; elapsed first-half calls remain unresolved where primary return data are missing.
speaker_map_notes: Dan Ives discusses technology fundamentals and named AI investments; Chris Verrone discusses market breadth, rotation and charts; Steve Eisman hosts and tests assumptions. Attribution follows extended turns; questions and agreement are scoped narrowly.
framework_points: Keep structural technology adoption separate from equity valuation and drawdowns.
Use bank participation and credit spreads as cross-market checks, while specifying signal rules before backtesting.
Challenge demand forecasts through power availability, monetization and funding.
Separate a conditional downside mechanism from a prediction that it will occur.
Use multi-year cash-flow scenarios without assuming every expensive stock will become a historical winner.
tools_and_charts: Bank stock breadth and credit spreads
Oracle RPO, FCF, debt and CDS
Treasury two/ten-year yields and 2 s 30 s curve
Palantir commercial revenue and FCF scenarios
transcript_cautions: Published January 5, 2026 but explicitly a 2025 year-end review; references to Micron reporting that day suggest late December 2025 recording. Exact date unconfirmed.
Captions switch to HH:MM:SS after one hour; the full 65-minute source was read.
Caption 2016 in healthcare outlook is contextually 2026; captions render IREN as iron, Fanuc as fuk and Palantir variously.
Three-person dialogue inferred from role and turns; ambiguous brief interjections are not used to create independent claims.
Opening montage and insurance advertisement excluded.
Exact market prices, chart levels and proprietary sentiment datasets were not independently reconstructed.
